Hi Sara / Peter —

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciate the context on FinPay's fraud-detection/claims routing use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the POC scope.

Recap from our call
- Primary workflows: real-time routing (sub-200ms 95th p50 target) + nightly batch re-scoring.
- Expected monthly usage: ~1.2B generated tokens (inference tokens), spike patterns around end-of-month reconciliation.
- Current cost sensitivity: looking to reduce per-1M-token unit cost vs your current hyperscaler spend while keeping latency SLAs.
- Important constraints: PCI-adjacent data, prefer VPC/private endpoints for production.

What we propose as next tests (2-week POC suggested)
1) Cost/TCO baseline: synthetic 1M-token run + model mix estimate (Llama-2-Chat-70B quantized + smaller 7B variants) to compute per-1M tokens with and without batching/cache.
2) Latency/load test: 50k requests at target concurrency to validate 95th percentile latency <200ms with our batching and routing settings.
3) Cache hit experiment: measure effective token reduction at different prefix/KV cache hit rates (20%, 40%, 60%).
4) Competitive comparison: run same synthetic workload against your current hyperscaler provider (Bedrock/OpenAI) to show delta in unit economics and tail latency.

I've attached a working cost model (redwood_tco_per_1M_tokens.xlsx) and an initial mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_finpay.pdf). The spreadsheet contains editable assumptions for batch size, sequence length distribution, and cache hit %.

Questions / asks from your side
- Can you share a representative payload (anonymized) for the real-time routing calls (sample prompt + average sequence lengths)?
- Who should we coordinate with for temporary test credentials for Bedrock/OpenAI so we can run the apples-to-apples cost tests?
- Are there regulatory/legal touchpoints we should loop in for the VPC/on-prem discussion?

Proposed timing: kickoff next Monday (7/20) for a two-week POC. If that works I can send a calendar invite and a short plan with success criteria.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Sara — great questions. See quick summary below (I put full line-item math in the attached spreadsheet for your procurement team).

Baseline assumptions (used in spreadsheet)
- Model mix: 70% 7B-class models (cost-efficient), 30% 70B-class chat model (quality-critical paths).
- Average input+output tokens per request: 420 tokens (prompt 120 + gen 300).
- Default batching: dynamic batching with coalescing window = 10ms, median batch size observed in similar customers = ~16 requests (sensitive to concurrency).
- KV/prefix cache: we treat prefix hits as reducing generated tokens billed; we also cache decoder KV so repeated prefixes avoid re-computation and reduce GPU time. Cache persistence: session affinity + warm-start heuristics reduce cold-starts; for longer-lived sessions KV persists in memory for the GPU worker (and we provide optional Redis-backed shared cache for Dedicated/Private deployments).

Quick per-1M-token economics (illustrative, see spreadsheet for full breakout)
- Redwood (baseline, no cache, batching applied): $12.40 per 1M generated tokens
- Redwood (with 40% cache hit assumed): effective $7.44 per 1M tokens (40% fewer billed/generated tokens)
- Redwood (high cache 60%): effective $4.96 per 1M tokens
- AWS Bedrock (our test harness estimates, public pricing blended): ~$20.50 per 1M tokens (no batching/caching adjustments in their hosted endpoint)
- OpenAI (gpt-4x-type estimate, blended): ~$26.00 per 1M tokens

Notes on batching vs quantization impact
- Batching primarily reduces per-token GPU amortized overhead and increases throughput; savings show up as lower $/token when request sizes and concurrency allow steady batch formation. For FinPay's traffic spike patterns we'll tune coalescing + auto-batching to hit the median batch sizes in the spreadsheet assumptions.
- Quantization reduces memory and may allow larger batch sizes on the same hardware; it also reduces per-token compute slightly depending on quant format. The spreadsheet models a conservative 10-15% compute savings from quantization on the 70B chat path.

Next steps I propose
1) We run a 1M-token synthetic baseline on Redwood and Bedrock/OpenAI using the exact request harness (you provide the anonymized payloads).
2) Run a 50k-request latency/load test to validate 95th <200ms with our runtime config.
3) Run cache-hit sweep (20/40/60%) and capture effective token reduction + latency impact.

If that sounds good I can send a short test-harness doc and a kickoff invite for Monday. Marcus (cc'd) will help with infra details and with the private/VPC checklist.

—Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
